name: BACH_0259
markdown:
## Bottom line
For biopsy case `BACH_0259`, the model predicts a **Benign** lesion (**99.8%** probability; **0%** invasive carcinoma risk) with a single-class 90% conformal prediction set (`["Benign"]`) and lowest worklist priority (**Tier 4**, unflagged) [F1]. A reviewer can place high initial trust in the benign category call—supported by **98%** image reliability [F6], cross-model consensus, and **5 of 5** similar reference cases [F5]—but should still inspect regions **9–11** on the slide, where segmented nuclei show high variation in nuclear size (**93rd** percentile) and shape (**100th** percentile) despite small average nuclear size (**5th** percentile) [F7, F8, F9].

## Confidence and uncertainty
This is a **confident call** on an image that passes quality control (`reliability_flag` = **false**, **12 of 12** regions kept vs. a minimum of **3**) [F6]. Because the prediction is unambiguous and unflagged (**Tier 4**), the case does not require urgent triage deferral, though standard diagnostic review of regions **9–11** is warranted to reconcile focal cytologic variability with the global benign prediction.

The classifier (`uni2h_lr`) assigns **99.83%** calibrated probability (**99.8%** in [F1]) to `Benign`, **0.13%** to `InSitu`, **0.04%** to `Normal`, and **0%** to `Invasive` (`risk_score` = **0.0**, with **0.0** invasive risk in all **12** regions) [F1]. These probabilities represent BACH diagnostic categories rather than Nottingham histologic grade; "aggressiveness" here refers strictly to the probability of invasive carcinoma (**0%**). At `conformal_alpha` = **0.10**, the split-conformal prediction set contains only `["Benign"]` [F1], meaning that across exchangeable test cases, the true class falls inside the prediction set about **90%** of the time; this is a dataset-level coverage guarantee, not a per-case probability, and a single-class set indicates the model separates `Benign` from the other three categories at that threshold. Two independent foundation models (CONCH and MUSK) agree on the top class (`conch_musk_same_top` = **true**), and all **5 of 5** nearest reference cases (**100%** `neighbor_agreement`; similarity **0.771–0.815**) are labeled `Benign` [F5], whereas the nearest contrasting case (`BACH_0135`, labeled `Normal`) has lower similarity (**0.705**). While image reliability is **98%** (`0.977`), `ood_percentile` is **1.0** (**100th** percentile) [F6], indicating that feature distance is at the upper end of the reference distribution even though quality screening did not flag the image as degraded.

| Signal | Value | What it means |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Top class & calibrated probabilities [F1] | **Benign** (**99.83%**); `InSitu` **0.13%**, `Normal` **0.04%**, `Invasive` **0%** | Near-certain separation in favor of a benign lesion with **0%** invasive risk (`risk_score` = **0.0**). |
| 90% conformal set (`alpha` = **0.10**) [F1] | `["Benign"]` (**1** class) | Single-class set under a **90%** dataset-level coverage guarantee; other classes are excluded at this error rate. |
| Image quality & reliability [F6] | Reliability **98%** (`0.977`); `reliability_flag` = **false**; **12/12** regions kept; OOD percentile **100%** (`1.0`) | All regions pass quality control without blur or stain flags, though the embedding sits at the **100th** OOD percentile. |
| Foundation model agreement | `conch_musk_same_top` = **true** | Independent foundation models (CONCH and MUSK) concur on the top diagnostic category. |
| Reference neighbor agreement [F5] | **5 of 5** (**100%**) `Benign` (similarity **0.771–0.815**) | Nearest cases (`BACH_0049`, `BACH_0387`, `BACH_0054`, `BACH_0123`, `BACH_0329`) are all `Benign`; nearest `Normal` contrast (`BACH_0135`) is at **0.705**. |
| Worklist priority | **Tier 4**, `flagged` = **false** | Lowest triage priority; no automated exception flags triggered. |

## Tissue evidence behind the call
The output reflects two distinct sources of tissue information: **model-derived concept scores** (linear concept-activation or text-prompt projections in embedding space, which are model scores rather than physical measurements) and **HoVer-Net cell measurements** (direct nuclear segmentation counts and morphometry, measured only on regions **9, 10, and 11**).

### Model-derived concept scores
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat (`benign_stroma_fat`) [F2]:** Scored at **1.44** (above typical) and strongest in regions **1, 5, and 7** (regional scores **1.28**, **1.63**, and **1.41**). It provides the largest push away from invasive carcinoma (contribution **-1.077**). Biologically, abundant intact collagenous or adipose stroma lacking desmoplasia supports a benign process over stromal invasion.
- **Gland / tubule formation (`tubules`) [F3]:** Scored from text embeddings at **2.157** (above typical; `cav_z` is null and `caption_consistent` is **false**), strongest in regions **1, 4, and 8** (regional scores **2.25**, **2.07**, and **2.16**, with a drop to **0.39** in region **9**). It provides the second-largest push away from invasive carcinoma (contribution **-0.978**). Preserved tubular and glandular architecture is biologically consistent with benign ductal/lobular parenchyma rather than solid or infiltrating carcinoma.
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate (`lymphocytes`) [F4]:** Scored at **1.237** (above typical) in regions **4, 5, and 10** (regional scores **1.16**, **1.44**, and **1.10**). Its direction is marked **context** (descriptive only, though its linear contribution term is **-0.846**). However, because this concept failed dataset-level spot-check validation (**8/20**, **40%** acceptable), this embedding score is **unreliable**.
- **Low stromal invasion and nuclear pleomorphism (`invasion`, `pleomorphism`):** `invasion` ("Tumor infiltrating stroma") is below typical at **-0.277** (negative across all **12** regions; least negative in region **5** at **-0.17**), pushing away from invasive carcinoma (contribution **-0.768**). `pleomorphism` ("Marked nuclear pleomorphism") is also below typical at **-0.832** (highest in region **4** at **-0.68**), pushing slightly away from invasion (contribution **-0.158**). Biologically, the absence of irregular stromal infiltration and marked cytologic atypia argues against invasive malignancy.
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts (`duct_confined`):** Scored at **0.492**, peaking in region **9** (**0.82**), with a small positive contribution (**+0.174**) toward invasive risk.
- **Unreliable concepts (`normal_lobules`, `mitoses`, `necrosis`):** `normal_lobules` (value **-0.15**, region **4**, contribution **+0.642** toward invasive risk due to lower-than-typical normal lobular signal), `mitoses` (value **-1.002**, region **4**, contribution **-0.491**), and `necrosis` (value **0.154**, region **9** score **0.54**, contribution **-0.079**) are all **unreliable** because they failed AI spot-check validation (**0/20**, **0/20**, and **3/20** acceptable, respectively) and should not be used to interpret the tissue.

### Measured cell features (HoVer-Net on regions 9, 10, and 11)
HoVer-Net (`hovernet_fast-pannuke` at **0.25** mpp) segmented **197** nuclei across regions **9, 10, and 11** (`contribution` = `null` for all cell features, meaning they do not directly weight the classifier's prediction): **41** neoplastic (region **9**: **13**, region **10**: **13**, region **11**: **15**; `neo_fraction` **21%** at the **65th** reference percentile; `neo_density` **303 per mm²** at the **55th** percentile), **57** epithelial (`epi_fraction` **29%**, **50th** percentile), **44** connective, **55** inflammatory, and **0** dead (`dead_fraction` **0%**, **22nd** percentile).
- **Small mean nuclear size (`nuc_area_mean`) [F7]:** Measured at **49.0 µm²** in regions **9, 10, and 11**, placing it at the **5th** percentile of benign reference cases (only **5%** of benign references have smaller nuclei). Small nuclear size is biologically typical of resting or benign epithelial and stromal cells rather than enlarged malignant nuclei.
- **High nuclear size and shape variation (`nuc_area_cv`, `nuc_shape_cv`) [F8, F9]:** In regions **9, 10, and 11**, variation in nuclear size is **0.5927** (**93rd** benign percentile) [F8] and variation in nuclear shape is **0.205** (**100th** benign percentile) [F9]. In a benign lesion, high apparent anisonucleosis and shape irregularity can arise from a mixture of compressed ductal, myoepithelial, stromal, and inflammatory nuclei, though true cytologic atypia must be ruled out on the glass/digital slide.
- **Immune cell fraction and spatial relation (`infl_fraction`, `til_proximity`) [F10]:** Inflammatory cells account for **28%** (`0.2792`) of nuclei in regions **9–11** (**100th** percentile of benign references) [F10], concentrated in region **10** (**42** inflammatory cells) and region **11** (**13** inflammatory cells) compared with region **9** (**0** inflammatory cells). The `til_proximity` score is **0.6182** (**68th** percentile), indicating moderate spatial proximity between lymphocytes and cells segmented as neoplastic.

## How far to trust these explanations
- **Calibrated probabilities, conformal sets, and reliability screening passed dataset-level checks (on a small test set):** On `n` = **132** test cases (**24** patient groups), post-calibration expected calibration error (ECE) is **5%** (`0.0548`, 95% CI **4%–22%**), and conformal prediction at `alpha` = **0.10** achieved **90%** coverage (`0.9015`, 95% CI **76%–98%**) with a mean set size of **1.31** (95% CI **1.18–1.38**). On **1,716** simulated frozen sections, the reliability score ranked misclassified cases with an AUROC of **0.70** (`0.7049`, 95% CI **0.59–0.86**).
- **The regional risk heatmap passed the deletion faithfulness test, whereas concept attributions did not:** In `uni2h_lr` (`n` = **132**), removing the **3** highest-risk regions produced a statistically significant drop in `P(invasive)` compared with random removal (`risk_minus_random` = **0.0114**, 95% CI **0.0021 to 0.0197**, excluding **0**), showing the spatial risk map (here **0.0** across all **12** regions) is faithful to the classifier. Removing the top **3** concept-ranked regions did not differ from random removal (`concept_minus_random` = **0.0008**, 95% CI **-0.0088 to 0.0064**, including **0**), demonstrating that concept scores are not proven to reflect what the classifier actually used.
- **Primary benign concepts passed AI spot checks, with one caveat:** In spot checks performed by an AI reviewer (not a pathologist), `benign_stroma_fat` [F2] was acceptable in **20/20** (**100%**) top regions and `tubules` [F3] in **18/20** (**90%**), and both showed pathology-consistent class directions (`direction_consistent` = **true**), though in this case `tubules` is derived solely from text embeddings and flagged as `caption_consistent` = **false**. `invasion` (**19/20**, **95%**) and `pleomorphism` (**18/20**, **90%**) also passed AI spot checks.
- **Several concepts scored in this case failed AI spot checks and are unreliable:** `lymphocytes` [F4] was acceptable in only **8/20** (**40%**) spot checks (with `direction_consistent` = `null`), `duct_confined` in **12/20** (**60%**), `necrosis` in **3/20** (**15%**), and both `normal_lobules` (**0/20**, **0%**) and `mitoses` (**0/20**, **0%**, also flagged `weak` = **true**) failed completely; these unreliable concepts also account for the reported contrast (`differs_most_in`) against `Normal` case `BACH_0135`.
- **Measured cell features have moderate validation:** HoVer-Net nuclei segmentations were acceptable in **15/21** (**71%**) AI spot checks, though `dead_fraction` and `epi_fraction` exhibited wrong-direction behavior at the dataset level.

The reviewer should therefore lean on the calibrated class probabilities [F1], the uniform **0.0** regional risk map, the **5 of 5** matched reference cases [F5], and the direct nuclear morphometry in regions **9–11** [F7–F10], while treating all concept attributions—and especially the unreliable `lymphocytes` [F4], `normal_lobules`, `mitoses`, and `necrosis` scores—as hypotheses only.

## Where the evidence disagrees
- **High nuclear size/shape variation and "neoplastic" cell labels vs. the benign call:** Despite a **99.8%** `Benign` probability [F1] and a low embedding `pleomorphism` score (**-0.832**), HoVer-Net labels **41** nuclei (**21%**) across regions **9, 10, and 11** as neoplastic and records nuclear size variation at the **93rd** benign percentile [F8] and nuclear shape variation at the **100th** benign percentile [F9]. At the same time, mean nuclear area is very small (**49.0 µm²**, **5th** percentile) [F7], suggesting HoVer-Net may be misclassifying benign proliferative epithelium, myoepithelial cells, or inflammatory/stromal nuclei as neoplastic and pleomorphic.
- **Focal atypical/intraductal signal in region 9:** Unlike the rest of the image where `tubules` scores **1.61–2.25**, region **9** shows a sharp drop in `tubules` (**0.39**) alongside the highest `duct_confined` score (**0.82**, pushing risk up by **+0.174**). `InSitu` is also the second-ranked class probability, though very small (**0.13%**).
- **Incomplete spatial sampling of cells and OOD percentile:** HoVer-Net cell segmentation was performed on only **3 of 12** regions (regions **9, 10, and 11**), leaving regions **0–8** (including the top concept regions **1, 4, 5, 7, and 8**) unmeasured at the cellular level. Furthermore, `ood_percentile` is **1.0** (**100th** percentile) despite a **98%** reliability score and `reliability_flag` = **false** [F6].
- **How this case could be wrong:** The case could be a false negative if region **9** (and adjacent regions **10–11**) harbors a focal **in situ proliferation (DCIS) or atypical ductal hyperplasia** masked by predominantly benign surrounding tissue, or if a **well-differentiated / small-cell invasive carcinoma** (such as tubular carcinoma in regions **1, 4, and 8** or low-grade invasive lobular carcinoma with small **5th**-percentile nuclei and **100th**-percentile shape variation in regions **9–11**) was misclassified as benign glands and stroma. Alternatively, it could represent normal breast lobules (`Normal` contrast case `BACH_0135` has **0.705** similarity, separated only by the unreliable `normal_lobules` and `mitoses` concepts) accompanied by benign chronic inflammation.

## What to check on the slide
1. **Region 9 (and adjacent regions 10 and 11) — intraductal architecture and nuclear atypia:** Examine the ducts and cell populations where HoVer-Net found **100th**-percentile nuclear shape variation (`0.205`) [F9], **93rd**-percentile size variation (`0.5927`) [F8], and **13–15** cells per region labeled neoplastic, and where `tubules` drops to **0.39** while `duct_confined` peaks at **0.82**. Finding small, uniform benign ductal and myoepithelial nuclei (consistent with the **49.0 µm²** mean area [F7]) confirms `Benign`; finding a clonal intraductal proliferation with true cytologic atypia or architectural rigidity would shift the diagnosis toward `InSitu` (or atypical hyperplasia).
2. **Regions 1, 4, and 8 — gland and tubule morphology:** Inspect the tubular structures driving the highest `tubules` scores (**2.25**, **2.07**, and **2.16**) [F3]. Confirming lobulocentric glands with an intact two-cell (luminal and myoepithelial) layer and basement membrane supports a benign lesion (or `Normal` lobules), whereas haphazard, angulated, single-layered open tubules infiltrating stroma would overturn the call toward tubular carcinoma.
3. **Regions 1, 5, and 7 — stroma and epithelial-stromal interface:** Check the fibrofatty background where `benign_stroma_fat` is strongest (**1.28**, **1.63**, and **1.41**) [F2] and region **5** (where `invasion` is least negative at **-0.17**). Bland fibrous/adipose tissue without desmoplasia or infiltrating cords confirms the **0%** invasive risk [F1], while discohesive small cells infiltrating stroma would overturn the benign prediction.
4. **Regions 10 and 11 (and regions 4 and 5) — lymphocytic infiltrate:** Evaluate the **42** and **13** inflammatory nuclei segmented in regions **10 and 11** (`infl_fraction` **28%**, **100th** benign percentile) [F10] alongside regions **4 and 5** (flagged by the unreliable `lymphocytes` concept [F4]). Confirming benign periductal or lobulocentric chronic inflammation explains the elevated immune fraction and nuclear shape variation, whereas lymphoid aggregates cuffing atypical ducts or infiltrating cords would warrant closer inspection for adjacent neoplasia.

## Limits
Sepia is a research prototype and has not been clinically validated for diagnostic or triage use. Its regional scores, concept activations, and nuclear measurements describe model behavior and serve only as hypotheses for the reviewing pathologist to verify on the slide, not proof of biological mechanism or diagnostic truth.
